_about: Material cards for pk_materials. Every value is {value, unit, source, honesty}; honesty in {standard_value, datasheet, typical_range, derived}. A typical_range value is the midpoint and carries its range. Densities are what mass_g multiplies by; the rest is what a check reads. A card may be `anisotropic`, in which case it names directions in its property keys (E_0, tensile_90) and lists in `refuses` the isotropic scalars it will not invent, each with the reason and the fix.

abs.notes: Same printing caveat as pla: bulk figures, 100% solid assumed.

aluminium_6061.notes: EN 1999-1-1 3.2.5 prints rho 2700 and E 70000 as design values for all wrought alloys, but that text was not fetched this session, so nothing here is claimed as standard. Yield is temper-dependent; the T6 range is served.

aluminium_6082.notes: Same caveat as aluminium_6061: EN 1999-1-1 design values not fetched, so served as a handbook range. Yield is temper-dependent; the T6 range is served.

density.source: Smith Metals 7075 Aluminium technical datasheet, mechanical + physical property tables; density 2.81 g/cm3

E.source: Smith Metals 7075 Aluminium technical datasheet, mechanical + physical property tables; modulus of elasticity 72 GPa

yield.source: Smith Metals 7075 Aluminium technical datasheet, mechanical + physical property tables; 'up to 465 MPa yield strength ... depending on temper', i.e. the T6 peak - the sheet does not tabulate per temper

tensile.source: Smith Metals 7075 Aluminium technical datasheet, mechanical + physical property tables; 'up to ... 540 MPa tensile strength', corroborated by its own 78 ksi upper bound (538 MPa)

aluminium_7075_t6.notes: THE SOURCE CONTRADICTS ITSELF ON YIELD and this card follows the self-consistent half. It prints 'Yield Strength 24-68 ksi, 455-465 MPa'; 24-68 ksi is 165-469 MPa, so the MPa range cannot be the same quantity - the ksi range spans tempers from annealed while the MPa figures are the T6 end. Its tensile line IS consistent (40-78 ksi = 275-540 MPa), and 68 ksi = 469 MPa agrees with the 465 quoted in its own prose, so the T6 values are taken and the annealed end is not served. 7075 is roughly TWICE the yield of 6061 at the same stiffness and 4% more weight, and it is chosen where corrosion resistance is not the concern - the datasheet says so itself.

brass_cw614n.notes: Lead content makes CW614N RoHS-exempt only under specific annexes; the card carries mechanics, not compliance.

cfrp_as4_8552_qi.designation: AS4/8552 quasi-isotropic layup, e.g. [0/+45/-45/90]s, fibre volume 57.42%

density.source: Hexcel HexPly 8552 product data sheet (EU), physical + mechanical property tables, AS4 column, 25 C dry, UD Nominal Laminate Density 1.58 g/cm3; stacking sequence does not change density, so the same plies quasi-isotropically stacked weigh the same

E.source: classical laminate theory, in-plane invariants U1 = (3Q11+3Q22+2Q12+4Q66)/8 and U4 = (Q11+Q22+6Q12-4Q66)/8, E = (U1^2-U4^2)/U1, nu = U4/U1, evaluated on the AS4/8552 UD lamina E1 = 141 000 and E2 = 10 000 N/mm2 printed by Hexcel HexPly 8552 product data sheet (EU), physical + mechanical property tables, AS4 column, 25 C dry. G12 and nu12 are NOT on that datasheet, so they are swept over 4 000-8 500 N/mm2 and 0.25-0.35 - a factor of two in G12 - and the range below is that whole sweep: the answer moves 3.5%, because a quasi-isotropic laminate's in-plane stiffness is governed by E1 and E2

nu.source: classical laminate theory, in-plane invariants U1 = (3Q11+3Q22+2Q12+4Q66)/8 and U4 = (Q11+Q22+6Q12-4Q66)/8, E = (U1^2-U4^2)/U1, nu = U4/U1, evaluated on the AS4/8552 UD lamina E1 = 141 000 and E2 = 10 000 N/mm2 printed by Hexcel HexPly 8552 product data sheet (EU), physical + mechanical property tables, AS4 column, 25 C dry. G12 and nu12 are NOT on that datasheet, so they are swept over 4 000-8 500 N/mm2 and 0.25-0.35 - a factor of two in G12 - and the range below is that whole sweep: the answer moves 3.5%, because a quasi-isotropic laminate's in-plane stiffness is governed by E1 and E2

yield.reason: in-plane STIFFNESS is quasi-isotropic; strength is not. It depends on which ply fails first and therefore on the stacking sequence, which this card does not fix
yield.fix: read the UD card's tensile_0/tensile_90 and run a laminate failure criterion for your actual stack

G.reason: derivable as E/(2(1+nu)) BECAUSE the in-plane response is isotropic, but the datasheet prints no G12 to derive it from
G.fix: supply G12 and compute, or accept E/(2(1+nu)) yourself and say you did

cfrp_as4_8552_qi.notes: The one CFRP card that may serve a plain E and nu: a quasi-isotropic stack really is isotropic IN-PLANE, which is the whole point of the layup. It is NOT isotropic in bending - [0/45/-45/90]s and [90/45/-45/0]s share this E and have different bending stiffness because the plies sit at different distances from the mid-plane - and it is not isotropic through the thickness. Use this for in-plane membrane loads only.

cfrp_as4_8552_woven.designation: AS4 3K plain weave / HexPly 8552, fibre volume 55.29%

density.source: Hexcel HexPly 8552 product data sheet (EU), physical + mechanical property tables, AS4 column, 25 C dry, Nominal Laminate Density 1.57 g/cm3 (printed, not derived)

E_0.source: Hexcel HexPly 8552 product data sheet (EU), physical + mechanical property tables, AS4 column, 25 C dry, 0 deg tensile modulus

E_90.source: Hexcel HexPly 8552 product data sheet (EU), physical + mechanical property tables, AS4 column, 25 C dry, 90 deg tensile modulus

tensile_0.source: Hexcel HexPly 8552 product data sheet (EU), physical + mechanical property tables, AS4 column, 25 C dry, 0 deg tensile strength

compressive_0.source: Hexcel HexPly 8552 product data sheet (EU), physical + mechanical property tables, AS4 column, 25 C dry, 0 deg compression strength

E_compressive_0.source: Hexcel HexPly 8552 product data sheet (EU), physical + mechanical property tables, AS4 column, 25 C dry, 0 deg compression modulus

ilss.source: Hexcel HexPly 8552 product data sheet (EU), physical + mechanical property tables, AS4 column, 25 C dry, 0 deg ILSS, short-beam shear

E.reason: a 0/90 weave is BALANCED, not isotropic: 68 000 N/mm2 along the warp and 66 000 along the fill, but far softer at 45 deg, where the load goes into shear - and this datasheet prints no 45 deg value
E.fix: read E_0 and E_90, and if the load runs at 45 deg to the weave say so and supply a 45 deg value or a laminate calculation

yield.reason: CFRP breaks rather than yielding, and the strength is direction-dependent

G.reason: the sheet prints interlaminar shear (ILSS, short-beam) and no in-plane shear modulus
G.fix: read ilss for the interlaminar strength; supply G_12 from your own laminate data

nu.fix: supply nu from your own laminate data

cfrp_as4_8552_woven.notes: Balanced 0/90, which is why E_0 and E_90 are within 3% - and exactly why a single E is still wrong: rotate the load 45 deg and a plain weave is far softer. The second fabric style in the same table (5HS) reads 67/66 GPa, so the weave style barely moves the in-plane numbers; the drape and the thickness are what change.

cfrp_hec_se75_ud.notes: The carbon UD card whose transverse numbers are MEASURED rather than refused - compare cfrp_t300_ud, built from Toray's fibre sheet, which has to refuse E_90 because a fibre datasheet cannot supply it. The two densities agree to 1.3% (1526 here against 1546 there) by independent routes, which is a useful check on both.

density.source: rule of mixtures at the datasheet's own basis: 0.60 x 1760 (T300 fibre, Toray TORAYCA T300 data sheet, Rev. 04/22/2025 (composite values normalized to 60% fibre volume, cured with #2500 epoxy at 130 C)) + 0.40 x rho_matrix, rho_matrix 1150-1300 kg/m3 for a cured laminating epoxy; the range below is that assumption's whole span

tensile_0.source: Toray TORAYCA T300 data sheet, Rev. 04/22/2025 (composite values normalized to 60% fibre volume, cured with #2500 epoxy at 130 C), tensile strength ASTM D3039

tensile_90.source: Toray TORAYCA T300 data sheet, Rev. 04/22/2025 (composite values normalized to 60% fibre volume, cured with #2500 epoxy at 130 C), 90 deg tensile strength ASTM D3039

shear_ip.source: Toray TORAYCA T300 data sheet, Rev. 04/22/2025 (composite values normalized to 60% fibre volume, cured with #2500 epoxy at 130 C), in-plane shear strength ASTM D3518

E.reason: a laminate has no single Young's modulus: this card serves E_0 = 140 000 N/mm2 along the fibres, and across them it is roughly a tenth of that
E.fix: read E_0, or give the layup and ask for the laminate's own modulus

yield.reason: CFRP does not yield, it breaks, and the strength depends on the direction: the same datasheet prints 1820 N/mm2 along the fibres and 76 across them, a factor of 24
yield.fix: read tensile_0, tensile_90 or compressive_0 and say which direction the load takes

G.reason: shear is in-plane, interlaminar or transverse and they are different numbers

nu.reason: a UD laminate has two Poisson's ratios (nu_12 and nu_21) and this datasheet prints neither
nu.fix: supply nu_12 from your own laminate data

cfrp_t300_ud.notes: UNIDIRECTIONAL, and that is the least representative layup for a real part: a woven or quasi-isotropic laminate of the same fibre is far stiffer across the part and far less stiff along it. Density is what the kernel uses for mass and is direction-free; every stiffness and strength here is the 0 deg value unless its name says otherwise.

stainless_1_4404.notes: TYPICAL values, not specified minima - the distinction the steel cards carry the other way round, where ReH is a minimum. EN 10088-2 sets materially lower minima for this grade, so a design to the standard must use those and not this 300. The molybdenum is the whole point: 316 resists chlorides where 1.4301 (304) pits, which is why the two must not share a name. Aperam prints 1.4401 and 1.4404 in one row, so this card does not distinguish 316 from low-carbon 316L; if the weld sensitisation matters to you, that difference is real and this card does not carry it.

steel_100cr6.notes: Strength depends entirely on heat treatment (annealed vs through-hardened 60+ HRC), so no yield is claimed.

titanium_grade2.notes: Unalloyed titanium: about a THIRD the yield of Ti-6Al-4V (276 against 869 N/mm2) at nearly the same density, so it is chosen for corrosion resistance, formability and weldability rather than strength - seawater, heat exchangers, pressure vessels. The same data sheet also covers Grade 2H, which is Grade 2 held to a higher 58 ksi minimum tensile with the same 40 ksi yield; that is a different column and would be a different card. Unlike the Ti-6Al-4V sheet, this one prints a Poisson ratio.

titanium_ti6al4v.notes: Strengths are SPECIFIED MINIMA, not typical values - the same distinction the steel cards carry - and they drop with thickness exactly as steel's ReH does: above 0.1874 in AMS 4911 specifies 130 ksi tensile and 120 ksi yield, so a thick plate is weaker than this card says. Typical annealed bar runs 138-155 ksi tensile. Solution treated and aged material is stronger again (150-172 ksi) and is a different card if you need it.
